data.subject: NYSE - New Security Notification for Symbol PS
data.body:
NYSE has determined that the Common Stock issued by Pershing Square Inc. is part of a new security offering that will trade under the ticker PS with CUSIP 71531U102 on April 29, 2026. As this new offering has not previously traded on any listing market and has no prior day's closing price, Regulation SHO Rule 201 will not apply to security PS until its second day of trading on NYSE. Further, NYSE Rule 123D(d) will apply and the security will be in a regulatory halt until the NYSE has opened trading.

Pershing Square Inc (NYSE: PS) is distributed without additional consideration to investors in the IPO of Pershing Square USA, Ltd. (NYSE: PSUS), closed‑end fund, with pricing anticipated on April 28, 2026 and listing on April 29, 2026. The two securities will trade separately.

data.subject: NYSE Arca Options - NYSE Pillar Hardware Upgrade - Update
data.body:
On June 1, 2026, NYSE Arca Options will upgrade hardware for its NYSE Pillar technology platform, as previously announced. The migration will be an immediate cutover, with no parallel production period. The certification environment will be available beginning April 27, 2026. 

Key Updates 

  • New Proprietary Market Data TXN channels (17-24) will begin disseminating heartbeats in Production on June 1, 2026 with symbols on new channels to follow at a later date. 
  • The NYSE Proprietary Data IP Addresses file has been updates to include new Production channels and new Certification source IPs.

data.subject: 2026 Regulation SCI BCP/DR Testing - October 24, 2026
data.body:
On October 24, 2026, NYSE, NYSE American, NYSE American Options, NYSE Arca, NYSE Arca Options, NYSE Bonds, NYSE Texas, NYSE National, and FINRA/NYSE TRF® (collectively, "NYSE") will conduct business continuity and disaster recovery testing during the SIFMA coordinated industry test. Market participants that meet criteria established by the NYSE exchanges for designation as a required participant ("Required Participants") will be notified by NYSE in April 2026.  

In preparation for the October 24th test, the NYSE will make the Cermak Disaster Recovery ("DR") environments available for connectivity testing on September 26, 2026 and October 10, 2026.The test hours for the two pre-tests and the test itself are 8:30am to 12:00pm ET. 

Testing Requirements 

Participating firms, including all Required Participants, must confirm participation (whether successful or not) by: 

  • Connecting to NYSE's Cermak DR site from the firm's Production or DR site; 
  • Sending an order or quote (NYSE will route to participating exchanges during the test);  
  • Testing ability to receive market data; and 
  • Completing an NYSE RegSCI DR Test - Firm Participation Form ("Checklist")  
  • The Checklist will be provided to participating firms in advance of the test.  
  • Upon receipt of the Checklist, NYSE will provide firms with a "confirmation of test completion" email to a contact provided by the firm on the Checklist. 

Required Participants 

Required Participants will be designated pursuant to the criteria set forth below, which are intended to identify the firms that, taken as a whole, represent the minimum necessary for the maintenance of fair and orderly markets in the event of the activation of business continuity and disaster recovery plans: 

  • Required Participants for the NYSE, NYSE American, NYSE Arca, NYSE Texas and NYSE National equities markets are (i) each firm that executed 3% or more of the applicable exchange's aggregate daily volume over a three-month period and (ii) all firms that are active Lead Market Makers (LMM) on NYSE Arca, Designated Market Makers (DMM) on NYSE, electronic Designated Market Makers (e-DMMs) on NYSE American, or Supplemental Liquidity Providers (SLP/SLMM) on NYSE.  
  • Required Participants for the NYSE American Options and NYSE Arca Options markets are (i) each firm (ATP or OTP holders) that executed 3% or greater of the applicable exchange's aggregate electronic average daily volume over a three-month period and (ii) all firms that are Lead Market Makers (LMM) on NYSE Arca Options or Specialists/E-Specialists on NYSE American Options. 
  • Required Participants for the Bonds market are each member organization that executed 20% or more of the market's aggregate daily volume over a three-month period. 

NYSE will announce any further modifications to Required Participant criteria by Trader Update and will designate and notify Required Participants at least three months in advance of the scheduled test.  

Additionally, all NYSE exchanges mandate that SCI Required Participants also participate in one Market Wide Circuit Breaker Test within the year. The dates of the 2026 MWCB tests are April 11, July 25, September 12, and December 5, 2026. 

Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with any questions regarding this update.

data.subject: NYSE Arca Options - NYSE Pillar Hardware Upgrade
data.body:
On June 1, 2026, NYSE Arca Options will upgrade hardware for its NYSE Pillar technology platform. The migration will be an immediate cutover, with no parallel production period. There are no changes to specifications or sessions with this upgrade. 

The certification environment will be available beginning April 27, 2026.  

Proprietary Market Data Feeds 

NYSE Arca Options Top (BBO and Trades), Deep and Complex (excluding Imbalance and Summary) feeds will increase from 17 to 24 Publisher, Refresh and Retransmission channels. 

NYSE Arca Options Certification Source IPs will be changing with the hardware upgrade. Please refer to NYSE Proprietary Data IP Addresses for new Certification source IPs. New Production channel information will be provided in a future trader update.  

Customers should use the start of day symbol reference data for symbol mapping information. There will be no XDP format changes. 

Key Dates

Certification environment available 

Monday, April 27, 2026 

Industry Test #1 

Saturday, May 16, 2026 

Industry Test #2 

Saturday, May 30, 2026 

New Hardware in Production 

Monday, June 1, 2026 


Market Data channel and DR hardware changes will be announced at a later date.

Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with any questions about this update.

data.subject: NYSE Arca Options and NYSE American Options – Monday / Wednesday Expirations for Qualifying Securities
data.body:
NYSE American Options and NYSE Arca Options are expanding the Short Term Options Series Program to permit the listing of up to two Monday and Wednesday expirations in addition to the Friday weekly expiration for Qualifying Securities. 

To qualify, a security must meet the following requirements on a quarterly basis: 

  • Individual stocks must have a market capitalization exceeding $700 billion (based on closing price), or 
  • Exchange Traded Funds (ETF) must have Assets under Management (AUM) exceeding $50 billion (based on net asset value) 

Additionally, 

  • Monthly options volume exceeding 10 million contracts (measured by sides traded in the final month of the preceding quarter) 
  • A position limit of at least 250,000 contracts, and 
  • Participation in the Penny Interval Program 

Each calendar quarter, the Exchange will evaluate individual stocks and ETFs to determine eligibility for the following quarter as a Qualifying Security. The Exchange will make the list of Qualifying Securities available by close of business on the first trading day of the quarter. Qualifying Securities that do not continue to meet the above criteria would no longer be permitted to list Monday and Wednesday expiries beginning on the second day of the following quarter.

data.subject: NYSE Group: Market Wide Circuit Breaker Test April 11, 2026
data.body:
On Saturday, April 11, 2026, NYSE, NYSE American, NYSE Arca, NYSE National and NYSE Texas will participate in the Securities Information Processors' (SIPs) industry testing of Market-Wide Circuit Breaker (MWCB) Level 1 and 2. NYSE Group equities markets will be available from their primary data sites in Mahwah from 9:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. ET. 

Designated required participants for the October 2026 Reg. SCI test on NYSE, NYSE American, NYSE Arca, NYSE National and NYSE Texas are required to participate in at least one MWCB test, per year.  Firms will be notified of their requirement in April 2026. 

The script for the test can be found here. The testing requirements below must be completed for each NYSE Group equities exchange for which a firm has been designated as a required tester: 

  • Receive and process MWCB halt messages from the SIPs. 
  • Receive and process resume messages from the SIPs following a MWCB halt. 
  • Receive and process market data from the SIPs relevant to the MWCB halt. 
  • Send orders following a Level 1 or Level 2 MWCB halt in a manner consistent with usual trading behavior. 

Firms should register to test at trading@nyse.com to have their participation recorded. Following the test, firms must return the participation checklist to Regscitesting@nyse.com. 

Remaining 2026 SIP Failover/MWCB Saturday Testing Dates 

  • April 11, 2026 - SIP Failover / MWCB Level 1/2 Test #1 
  • July 25, 2026 - SIP Failover / MWCB Level 1/2 Test #2 
  • September 12, 2026 - MWCB Level 1/2/3 Test  
  • December 5, 2026 - SIP Failover / MWCB Level 1/2 Test #3 

Please contact your NYSE Relationship Manager or rmteam@nyse.com with any questions about this test.

data.subject: NYSE Arca Equity Membership On-Ramp Program
data.body:
NYSE Arca has introduced a program for new Equity Trading Permit (ETP) Holders designed to reduce the cost of entry by providing tiered discounts on trading license fees, connectivity port fees, and select market data products (the "Program"). The Program offers graduated fee relief over an 18-month period, enabling new participants to scale into the NYSE Arca equities marketplace at a reduced cost 

Eligibility 

To qualify for the Program, a firm must not have been approved as an NYSE Arca ETP Holder within the prior 18 months. Each firm may enroll in the Program only once. Affiliates of existing ETP Holders (defined as any ETP Holder under 75% common ownership or control) are not eligible to participate. 

Discount Schedule 

Discounting begins in the calendar month in which the firm's new ETP membership application is approved. Eligible firms for the Program may receive the following tiered discounts: 

 

Category 

Months 1-6 Discount 

Months 7-12 Discount 

Months 13-18 Discount  

Trading Permit Fees 

100%  

50%  

25%  
Order Entry/Quote Entry Ports: Fees for the first 10 ports  100% 50% 25%

Drop Copy Ports: Fees for the first 10 ports 

100%  

50%  

25%  

Market Data Fees: 

· NYSE Arca Integrated Feed 

· NYSE Arca Book 

· NYSE Arca Aggregated Lite 

· NYSE Arca BBO 

· NYSE Arca Trades  

· NYSE Arca Order Imbalances 

100%  

50%  

25%  

 

  • The Market Data fees that are eligible for the Program are: Access Fees (general and Per User, if applicable), Professional User Fees (internal use only), Non-Professional User fee (for external use, including Enterprise Fees), Non-Display Fees, Redistribution Fee, and Multiple Data Feed Fee ("Eligible Market Data Fees"). The Program's discounts are not available to a ETP Holder subject to the Digital Media Enterprise Fee or Professional User Fees for any data externally distributed to professional subscribers. A firm that was a subscriber to any of the Eligible Market Data Fees within the prior 18 months before becoming approved as a new ETP holder is ineligible for Program's Market Data fee discounts. Program discounts cannot be combined with any other discounts applicable to Eligible Market Data Fees. 

 

Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with questions about this update.

data.subject: Regulatory Transaction Fee Rate Adjustment per SEC Section 31
data.body:

Until that date, the current rate of $0.00 per million dollars will remain in effect.

For additional details regarding the SEC's Fee Rate Advisory, please refer to the SEC's announcement at sec.gov.

data.subject: NYSE Group - NYSE Pillar and Trade Ops Portal (TOP) Improvements
data.body:
Beginning March 23, 2026, NYSE Group equities and options exchanges will implement performance improvements and introduce new functionality on NYSE Pillar and the NYSE Pillar Trade Ops Portal (TOP), including:

  • Repricing optimizations
  • Market data publication improvements
  • Max Notional Check for Complex Options
  • All market data sessions available in TOP GUI and REST API
  • Updates to outbound timestamp, as previously announced

Changes on NYSE Pillar are available for testing across NYSE Group equities and options certification environments. TOP functionality will be available for testing on April 20, 2026.

Repricing Optimizations (NYSE Equities and Options Markets)

Repricing logic will be optimized; functionality for repricing orders and quotes will not change.

Improvements to Market Data Publication (NYSE Equities Markets Only)

Market data updates will be improved by publishing executions and related updates incrementally as orders interact at each price level.

Max Notional Check for Complex Options (NYSE Options Markets Only)

The single-order notional check will be modified to use the Series Contract Multiplier as part of the calculation for Complex Orders. This change was previously applied to Single-Leg Orders in Q3 2025.

Market Data Sessions Available in TOP GUI and REST API (NYSE Equities and Options Markets)

All market data sessions will be available in the TOP GUI and REST API beginning on Monday, April 27, 2026.

data.subject: NYSE: Reminder - Direct Debit via DTCC and Invoice Changes Effective April 2026
data.body:
Beginning in April 2026, NYSE will transition to Direct Debit via DTCC ("Direct Debit") as the default payment method for certain fees and introduce a new invoice format that summarizes execution fees, as previously announced.

DTCC Direct Debit for Transaction, Membership, and Session Fees

The transition to Direct Debit for Transaction, Membership, and Session Fees will be implemented in April 2026.  Firms may opt out of Direct Debit by completing the Direct Debit Opt-Out Request form and returning it to CRS at crs@nyse.com by March 24, 2026.

Invoice Format Update

Beginning with the April 2026 bill, a new invoice format will be introduced that summarizes fees by the liquidity tag returned on executions.  A full list of liquidity tags may be found on the NYSE Pillar Reason Codes and Liquidity Indicators.

 

For questions about these changes, please contact rmteam@nyse.com.

data.subject: NYSE Arca - Fee Changes Effective March 2, 2026
data.body:
Effective March 2, 2026, pending effectiveness of regulatory filings, NYSE Arca will revise its fee schedule to:

  • Eliminate the $0.0029 fee for removing liquidity in Tape B for ETP Holders that qualify for Adding Tiers 1, 2, 3, 4, or 6.

  • Cap the Tape B credit for Step Up Tier 3 at $0.0031.

Tape B Remove Rate

ETP Holders that qualify for Adding Tiers 1 - 6 will be subject to the standard fee of $0.0030 for removing liquidity in Tape B.

Step Up Tier 3 - Maximum Tape B Credit

ETP Holders qualifying for Step Up Tier 3 will not be eligible to receive additional Tape B Tier credits for adding displayed liquidity, including any credits associated with Less Active ETP Securities. The maximum Tape B credit for Step Up Tier 3 will be $0.0031.

 

Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with questions about these changes.

data.subject: NYSE American Options - NYSE Pillar Hardware Upgrade Postponement
data.body:
The NYSE American Options hardware upgrade for the NYSE Pillar technology platform has been postponed to Monday, March 9, 2026. The migration will be an immediate cutover, with no parallel production period. 

Gateway IP Address Update

As part of this upgrade, the Exchange will not be redistributing gateways with the new hardware, as previously announced. Firms' current primary and secondary gateway IP addresses will remain as assigned.

Proprietary Market Data Feeds

NYSE American Options Top (BBO and Trades), Deep and Complex (excluding Imbalance and Summary) proprietary market data feeds will increase from 17 to 24 Publisher, Refresh and Retransmission channels. Please refer to NYSE Proprietary Data IP Addresses for new channel information. 

There will be no XDP format changes. Customers should use the start of day symbol reference data for symbol mapping information. 

Revised Timeline

 

Original Date

New Date

Industry Test #3

Saturday, February 28, 2026

Saturday, March 7, 2026

New Hardware in Production

Monday, March 2, 2026

Monday, March 9, 2026

DR Industry Test

data.subject: NYSE Arca Options: MXEA and MXEF MSCI Index Options Available for Trading on February 25, 2026
data.body:
Effective February 25, 2026, options on the MSCI EAFE Index (MXEA) and the MSCI Emerging Markets Index (MXEF) will be listed and available for trading on NYSE Arca Options.

NYSE's listing of MXEA and MXEF builds on ICE's decades-long partnership with MSCI, which includes providing the world's most liquid MSCI futures markets. 

Pending regulatory approval, NYSE American Options will list and trade MXEA and MXEF options in March, followed by additional MSCI index options on both NYSE options markets. 

For additional information, please visit https://www.nyse.com/trade/options/msci-global-index-options or contact rmteam@nyse.com.

data.subject: NYSE - Direct Debit via DTCC and Invoice Changes Effective April 2026
data.body:
Beginning in April 2026, NYSE will move to Direct Debit via DTCC ("Direct Debit") as the default payment method for certain fees and introduce a new invoice format that summarizes fees on executions. 

DTCC Direct Debit for Transaction, Membership, and Session Fees 

The previously announced move to Direct Debit via DTCC ("Direct Debit") for Transaction, Membership, and Session Fees will now be implemented in April 2026. 

Firms may opt out of Direct Debit by completing the Direct Debit Opt-Out Request form and returning it to CRS at crs@nyse.comby March 24, 2026. 

Invoice Format Update 

Beginning with the April 2026 bill, a new invoice format will be introduced. This updated format will summarize fees by the liquidity tag returned on executions.  A full list of liquidity tags may be found on the NYSE Pillar Reason Codes and Liquidity Indicators . 

Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with any questions about these changes.

data.subject: NYSE Arca Options - Cash-Settled FLEX ETF Options Available February 2026
data.body:
Beginning February 2, 2026, NYSE Arca Options will offer 'cash' settlement as a flexible term for select eligible issues, pursuant to NYSE Arca Options Rule 5.32-O(f). To qualify, the underlying ETF must have an average daily notional value of $500 million or more and a national average daily volume of at least 4,680,000 shares (measured over the prior 6-month period). If an underlying ETF ceases to satisfy the criteria, any new position overlying the ETF will only settle by physical delivery, and any open position may be traded only to close the position.

data.subject: NYSE Options: Optional NYSE Pillar Order Entry Restrictions
data.body:
Beginning February 2, 2026 on NYSE American Options and February 4, 2026 on NYSE Arca Options, the Exchanges will introduce optional order restrictions that firms may enable on the NYSE Pillar Gateway order entry sessions. Firms may activate any or all of the restrictions. This functionality will be available for testing on the NYSE Pillar Certification environment on January 26, 2026.

NYSE Pillar Options Order Entry Restrictions

Using the NYSE Pillar NGW Session Request Form, firms may configure their FIX and Binary order entry sessions with the following optional restrictions:

  • CustomerOrFirm
    Require a specific value in the CustomerOrFirm field at order entry.
    If CustomerOrFirm field contains any other value, Pillar will reject it with: R038: Invalid CustomerOrFirm.
  • CMTA/ClearingFirm
    Require a specific value in the CMTA/ClearingFirm field at order entry.
    If CMTA/ClearingFirm field contains a different value or is missing, Pillar will reject it with: R047: Invalid ClearingFirm.
  • Account/UserData
    Require an Account/UserData field be populated at order entry.
    If Account/UserData field is left blank, Pillar will reject the message with: R167: Invalid UserData.

Updated System Resources

  • NYSE Pillar Risk Controls
  • Functional Differences between NYSE Group Options Platforms
  • NYSE Pillar NGW Session Request Form

Please contact tms@nyse.com for certification testing or support@nyse.com for assistance with production.

data.subject: NYSE American Options - Cash-Settled FLEX ETF Options Changes Beginning February 2026
data.body:
Pursuant to NYSE American Options Rule 903G(c)(3)(ii), the Exchange offers 'cash' settlement as a flexible term for select eligible issues. To qualify, the underlying security must have an average daily notional value of $500 million or more and a national average daily volume of at least 4,680,000 shares (measured over the prior 6-month period). Beginning in March 2026, NYSE ("the Exchange") will move to Direct Debit via DTCC ("Direct Debit") as the default payment method for Transaction, Membership, and Session Fees. This convenient process will offer firms the ability to pay fees via automatic debit from the firm's clearing account at DTCC. 

Firms may opt out of Direct Debit by completing this form and returning it to CRS at crs@nyse.com by February 20, 2026.

Firms with multiple MPIDs must contact CRS to establish a default billing MPID and associated DTCC number, from which firm level fees will be collected. Firms that use the Universal Flip Process at DTCC should also contact CRS.

DTCC Direct Debit for Transaction, Membership, and Session Fees

The process for Direct Debit, beginning in March 2026 will be as follows:

  • The Exchange will send monthly electronic invoices, generally by the fifth business day of each month, for fees generated in the prior month.
  • The Exchange will subsequently initiate the debit of any fees due to the Exchange for the prior month on or about the 15th day of the month.
  • Firms can dispute an invoice in writing by the 15th of the month or the following business day if the 15th is not a business day.  If the disputed amount is $10,000 or greater, the Exchange will not include the disputed amount in the debit pending resolution of the dispute.

For further information please see https://www.nyse.com/trade/trading-information#direct-debit.

Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with any questions about this change.

data.subject: NYSE Group: Reminder - New Tier Calculation Process (SEC Rule 610 Changes), Effective February 2, 2026
data.body:
Beginning February 2, 2026, NYSE Group equities exchanges will calculate monthly pricing tiers based on the prior month's trading activity as required by recent SEC Rule 610 amendments, as previously announced. New members will receive base rates during their first month of trading. 

Existing Daily Tier Reports will continue to display T+1 volume activity; however, this data will now be used to determine the following month's rates. 

For additional information, please refer to the SEC Final Rule.  

Please contact your NYSE Relationship Manager or email rmteam@nyse.com with any questions about this update.

data.subject: NYSE Options: 2026 Penny Program Annual Rebalance
data.body:
Effective January 2, 2026, NYSE American Options and NYSE Arca Options ("NYSE Options", each an "Exchange") will update the list of issues in the Penny Interval Program for Options (the "Penny Program") pursuant to the Annual Review provided for in the Penny Program, as described below. Detailed changes to Penny Program issues can be found here.

Penny Program Annual Review

NYSE Options adopted the Penny Program on July 1, 2020, and pursuant to the same, an annual rebalancing is performed wherein the Exchange adjusts the Penny Program to reflect changes in trading activity since it was adopted. The rebalancing provides:

  • Additions to the Penny Program: Based on the Annual Review, any option class not in the Penny Program that is among the 300 most actively traded multiply listed option classes overlying securities priced below $200, or an index at an index level below $200, will be added to the Penny Program on the first trading day of January.
  • Removals from the Penny Program: Except as provided for issues subject to corporate action or having been added since the last rebalancing, based on the Annual Review, any option class in the Penny Program that falls outside the 425 most actively traded multiply listed option classes will be removed from the Penny Program on the first trading day of April.

Any option class added during the year because of activity following initial listing will be added on the first trading day of the month after it qualifies and will remain in the Penny Program for one full calendar year.

Any series in an option class participating in the Penny Program in which the underlying security has been delisted or are identified by OCC as ineligible for opening customer transactions, will continue to quote pursuant to the terms of the Penny Program until all such options have expired.

For more information about the Penny Program, see NYSE American Rule 960.1NY and NYSE Arca Rule 6.72A-O.

Contact Information

Questions regarding the Penny Interval Program for Options may be directed to the NYSE Trading Operations Desk at 212-896-2830 option 1, 2.

For any questions regarding this update, please contact rmteam@nyse.com.

data.subject: NYSE Arca - Updated Limit Up Limit Down Tier 1 ETP List
data.body:
NYSE Arca, in coordination with other listing exchanges, has updated the list of Exchange Traded Products eligible for Tier 1 of the Limit Up Limit Down program. The updated list of ETPs, effective January 2, 2026, as well as the additions and deletions from the current Tier 1 list, can be found here.

To determine eligibility as a Tier 1 NMS stock, all ETPs across multiple asset classes and issuers were sorted by notional consolidated average daily volume ("CADV"). The list included domestic equity, international equity, fixed income, currency, and commodities and futures but excluded leveraged ETPs. Notional CADV was calculated by multiplying daily volumes by closing prices each day of the measuring period and then averaging them for the period. The measurement period was the first day of the previous fiscal half year up until one week before the beginning of the next fiscal half year, in this case, 7/1/2025 to 12/22/2025. ETPs, including inverse ETPs, which traded over $2,000,000 CADV were eligible to be included as a Tier 1 NMS stock.

data.subject: NYSE Group: Market Data Enhancements for Fractional Share Quantity Reporting - Reminder
data.body:
Effective January 12, 2026, NYSE Group will modify market data feeds in support of changes to the fractional share quantity reporting and dissemination to the UTP and CTA Security Information Processors (SIPs), as previously announced.

Proprietary market data customers are encouraged to test in the NYSE Certification environment, which is currently available. Sample data is accessible here.

FINRA/NYSE TRF

Industry tests will be held on January 10 and February 7, 2026, for FINRA/NYSE TRF® firms to test fractional share reporting and for market data subscribers to validate proprietary product changes.

Proprietary Market Data Specifications

For additional details, please review the updated specifications:

  • NYSE Trades Specification
  • NYSE Best Quotes and Trades (BQT) Specification
  • NYSE Best Quotes and Trades (BQT) Cloud Streaming Specification
  • TAQ NYSE Trades Specification
  • Daily TAQ Specification*

*Daily TAQ changes will be implemented on February 23, 2026, in line with the industry date for support of fractional share quantity reporting to the UTP and CTA SIPs for NMS stocks.

Contact

Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with any questions about this update.

data.subject: NYSE American Options - NYSE Pillar Hardware Upgrade
data.body:
On Monday, March 2, 2026, NYSE American Options will upgrade hardware for its NYSE Pillar technology platform. The migration will be an immediate cutover, with no parallel production period.

The certification environment will be available beginning Monday, January 5, 2026. Additional dates can be found below.

With the new hardware, NYSE American Options will be redistributing the assigned gateways for approximately 50% of sessions. This will result in the designation of primary and secondary gateway IP addresses being reversed for those sessions. Firms may still connect to either IP address in production.  Firms can determine primary vs secondary designation on NYSE Trade Ops Portal (TOP) or the REST API.

Proprietary Market Data Feeds

NYSE American Options Top (BBO and Trades), Deep and Complex (excluding Imbalance and Summary) feeds will increase from 17 to 24 Publisher, Refresh and Retransmission channels.

NYSE American Options Certification Source IPs will be changing with the hardware upgrade. Please refer to NYSE Proprietary Data IP Addresses for new Certification source IPs and new channel information.

Customers should use the start of day symbol reference data for symbol mapping information. There will be no XDP format changes.

Key Dates

Certification environment available

Monday, January 5, 2026

Industry Test #1

Saturday, January 10, 2026

Industry Test #2

Saturday, February 7, 2026

Industry Test #3

Saturday, February 28, 2026

New Hardware in Production

Monday, March 2, 2026

Heartbeats on new market data channels

Monday, March 2, 2026

Test symbols on new market data channels

Monday, March 9, 2026

DR Industry Test

Saturday, March 28, 2026

New hardware in DR

Monday, March 30, 2026

Production symbols on new channels

Tuesday, March 31, 2026

Further information may be found in the FAQs.

data.subject: NYSE - Change to Closing D Order Fee Determination
data.body:
Effective December 5, 2025, pending effectiveness of a regulatory filing, NYSE will update the definition of "last modified" used to determine Closing D Order fees. The new definition will be the later of the order's entry time or its final modification for each individual D Order designated for the Close.

Currently, "last modified" is defined as the later of the order's entry time or the final modification for a D Order designated for the Close with the same broker badge, entering firm mnemonic, symbol and side.

There are no changes to the existing fees.

 

Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with questions about this update.

data.subject: NYSE American Options - December 2025 Pricing Changes, Options Regulatory Fee (“ORF”) Update
data.body:
Effective December 1, 2025, pending effectiveness of regulatory filings, NYSE American Options (the "Exchange") will implement the following pricing changes: 

  1. Modify the Electronic Customer Complex Orders criteria to qualify for certain Single-Leg CUBE auction Initiating Participant Credits. 
  1. Implement a waiver of the ORF for December 2025, as previously announced. 

Initiating Participant Single-Leg CUBE Auction Credits 

The criteria to qualify for an Initiating Participant Credit of ($0.30) per contract for Penny Issues and ($0.70) per contract for Non-Penny Issues in Single-Leg CUBE Auctions by executing Electronic Customer Complex Orders has been modified to 0.30% of TCADV in Electronic Customer Complex Orders, lowered from 0.40%. There is no change to the alternative qualifying criteria of executing at least 0.40% of TCADV in monthly Initiating Complex CUBE Orders (inclusive of AON Complex CUBE Orders).

The FINRA/NYSE TRF® does not chargeport fees.

data.subject: NYSE Group: Final 2025 Market Wide Circuit Breaker Test - December 6
data.body:
On Saturday, December 6, 2025, NYSE, NYSE American, NYSE Arca, NYSE National and NYSE Texas will participate in the Securities Information Processors' (SIPs) industry testing of Market-Wide Circuit Breaker (MWCB) Levels 1 and 2. NYSE Group equities markets will be available from their primary data sites in Mahwah from 8:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. ET. 

Firms are encouraged to test their ability to receive all messages associated with MWCB, including decline status, halt, and resume messages. Firms will also be able to participate in re-opening auctions following the MWCB halts. 

All firms notified as designated required participants for the 2025 Reg. SCI test on NYSE, NYSE American, NYSE Arca, NYSE National and NYSE Texas are required to participate in at least one MWCB test, per year.  

The script for the test can be found here. The testing requirements below must be completed for each NYSE Group equities exchange for which a firm has been designated as a required tester: 

  • Receive and process MWCB halt messages from the SIPs. 
  • Receive and process resume messages from the SIPs following a MWCB halt. 
  • Receive and process market data from the SIPs relevant to the MWCB halt. 
  • Send orders following a Level 1 or Level 2 MWCB halt in a manner consistent with usual trading behavior. 

Firms should register to test at trading@nyse.com to have their participation recorded. 

After the test, firms must return the participation checklist to Regscitesting@nyse.com.  

Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with any questions about the test.

data.subject: NYSE Arca Options - Proposal to List and Trade Certain Options on a Commodity-Based Trust Deemed Approved
data.body:
Effective today, November 13, 2025, NYSE Arca Options (NYSE Arca) rule proposal, SR-NYSEARCA-2025-16, is deemed approved.

On February 24, 2025, NYSE Arca filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC"), a proposed rule change to amend its listing rules at Rule 5.3-O to allow the listing and trading of options on interests in a Commodity-Based Trust. SR-NYSEARCA-2025-16 was published in the Federal Register on March 17, 2025.  After designating a longer period to act, on June 12, 2025, the SEC issued an order instituting proceedings.  On September 4, 2025, the SEC designated November 12, 2025, as the date by which to issue an order approving or disapproving SR-NYSEARCA-2025-16. The SEC did not act to either approve or disapprove SR-NYSEARCA-2025-16 on or before November 12, 2025, therefore the proposal is deemed approved as of November 13, 2025.

On November 7, 2025, during the government shutdown, NYSE Arca submitted an amendment to the proposal.  Based on consultation with SEC staff, NYSE Arca intends to reiterate that amendment through an immediately effective rule filing to codify the proposed rule text and update the Exchange's Rulebook once the SEC resumes normal operations.  In the meantime, NYSE Arca will act under the amended version.  As amended, NYSE Arca Rule 5.3-O(g)(x) will specify that NYSE Arca may list and trade interests in a Commodity-Based Trust that meets the generic criteria of NYSE Arca, Inc. Rule 8.201-E (Generic) provided the trust holds a single crypto asset. Further, a Commodity-Based Trust that meets the requirements of Rule 5.3-O(g)(x) must also satisfy the following requirements: (A) the total global supply of the underlying crypto asset held by the Commodity-Based Trust has an average daily market value of at least $700 million over the last 12 months; and (B) the crypto asset held by the Commodity-Based Trust underlies a derivatives contract that trades on a market with which the Exchange has a comprehensive surveillance sharing agreement, whether directly or through common membership in the Intermarket Surveillance Group.

For purposes of this rule, the term "crypto asset" means an asset that is generated, issued and/or transferred using a blockchain or similar distributive ledger technology network including, but not limited to, assets known as "tokens," "digital assets," "virtual currencies," and "coins" and that rely on cryptographic protocols.

Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with any questions about this update.

data.subject: NYSE Texas - NYSE Pillar Hardware Upgrade - Final Reminder
data.body:
As previously announced, NYSE Texas proprietary market data feeds have been enhanced from 6 to 8 transaction partition (TXN) channels in support of the NYSE Texas hardware upgrade.

Certification testing in UAT environment is currently available. New production TXN channels are currently disseminating heartbeats and test symbols.

The Disaster Recovery ("DR") environment will be available for connectivity testing on November 8, 2025, with cutover to new DR hardware on November 10, 2025.

Please refer to NYSE Proprietary Data IP Addresses for new channel information. Customers should use the start of day symbol reference data for symbol mapping information. There will be no changes to the Certification channels and no XDP format changes.

Key Dates

DR Industry Test November 8, 2025
New Hardware in DR November 10, 2025
Production symbols on new channels  November 11, 2025

Further information may be found in the FAQs.

Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with any questions about this update.
